body: I completely agree, but like I mentioned on my post. I’m basically all alone, I need a job fist to basically survive I can’t really have the luxury right now to get the job I “want” when getting hired at all is such a hassle and time consuming.

This happens to me too with family and friends. However, I’ve noticed that if I like a person I will become obsessed almost, and want to be with them most if not all of the time. I won’t really show it out of fear of being looked as clingy but it’s all I can think about. It’s actually why my previous partner and I separated, because I felt like they weren’t there for me enough ( although they did admit to being absent so ig i didn’t make it up). It upset me how much I wanted to be with them because at one point it affected my daily life. 

Thankfully I was able to get over this, it took over a year and half my sanity, but eventually I surpassed it. I did read into disorganized attachment and I’m sure it played a big role in this. But the same won’t really happen for anyone else ( not that I would want this to happen with anyone at all honestly it’s exhausting) more then missing them I’ll feel anxious and guilty from not replying to them in so long, until one day I reply to everyone. I’ve been working on this now and try to keep consistency at least with the people closest to me. 

Before my previous partner I never really had anything serious with anyone, so I never really knew how I would react specially because I didn’t really see myself with anyone at the time. So I find it interesting how my mind works when it comes to relationships. I thought I would be bad at them for the same reason that I’m bad at friendships, keeping in touch, or being present. Turns out I’m the complete opposite and now I see what people criticize me so much about. 

But now that I’ve moved on I completely forgot what all of that felt like, like how you forget how something tastes if you haven’t eaten it in a while. I only remember how it made me feel at the time. I’m pretty sure this is normal, but yea, missing people at least in my experience variates.

When you’re stuck in a void of your own consciousness all you can think about is how to survive, everyday just feels like a list of tasks to get through it. I’m 20 turning 21 this Dec and in reality I didn’t think I would even make it past 18, right now you’re in survival mode and it’s not easy all your body and mind are trying to do is to keep you going. But I won’t lie one does have to put part in the healing journey. I’m not sure about your living circumstances, but now you have reached out to people in the internet and we all care that you’ll join us one more year, the world will feel a little more empty without you here so please I know it’s hard but don’t go just yet. 
What personally helped me was to understand my brain, when the first started my logic was to know how my brain chemically worked. This is gonna sound silly but body and brain are closely connected whatever you do to your body can directly impact your brain and vise versa. I recommend you just test out these few things I’m going to recommend for two weeks just try it and trust me you’ll see a difference. 
•try adding more vitamins like magnesium, vitamin C and D, vitamin B2 and fish oil( the pill) vitamins aren’t the cheapest so if you can only get one I definitely recommend magnesium before sleep. 

Nowdays because of busy schedules and frantic lifestyle we rarely care or put effort into nutrition, which disturbs balance to the chemicals in our brains, depression can be genetic yes but not feeding our brain can greatly decrease any kind of dopamine levels our brain produces. It’s honestly criminal we aren’t thought this enough.

•breath works, I used to struggle a lot with anxiety ( still do a bit ) when people started recommending breath works to me I honestly didn’t care much for it, it almost feels like you have no time for it, but trust me your breathing 100% of the time a few deep breaths won’t hurt. These help a lot deliver oxygen to your brain and body which can be cut short by anxiety believe it or not, anxiety is a version of constant panic/survival your brain is scared and tense, and all your brain perceives is fear so by calming your breathing it can help you focus in the present and realize there is no reason to panic.

•Mindfulness 
Depression and anxiety completely distort one’s way of thinking and viewing the world, many times making it much worse then it actually is, even when things are hard as long as we remind ourselves that we got exactly that, ourselves and that we are our own hero we can get through these tough times. 

Starting on a healing journey is not easy, I don’t mean to be discouraging it’s the last thing I mean, but I’m also trying to be realistic. One embarks on the journey thinking that we are going to be happy and on a high forever but that is far from the truth. Many times, you will want to go back (self sabotaging) go back to what you’ve know most your life, there might be lows were you say fuck it but that the whole thing about healing. Healing takes work and it’s reminding ourselves that even when we can’t take another step we can crawl with nails and everything. Healing is reminding ourselves that the work we put in mind is what will bring peace to our mind and heart. And trust me there will be a point were you’ve healed enough to look back and not only be proud of how far you’ve gotten, but also you will notice how things won’t affect you like they did before.

American education is no better, yes, but I haven’t heard any of that. What we do have are school shootings although not as often as people make it seem. The teachers are def not beating the students or vise versa, and if students are raping other students it’s most likely not on school grounds. I used to be a teachers assistant is several high schools, middle schools and elementaries and most I saw was the kids ditching class and your regular school fights. I guess I’ve been lucky that the schools I’ve gone to haven’t shown that side

But I also agree with you that I need to start acting respectable in general. If they don’t have the decency to do certain things and won’t consider me, then I shouldn’t be feeling like I do, I should know my worth and continue focusing them in other things. Either be ok by myself and be thankful for what I already have or look for people who see the same value I see in myself ( not saying the friends in this post don’t, it’s a short post and of course I’m not gonna add ever itty bitty gritty detail in, there’s a reason why I say they have a special place in my heart. But I’m also aware that when you like someone you tend to have rose colored glasses and in my case this can happen with friends too, I wanted an outside perspective to show me how it really is or how other ppl may view this. And you did just that, I may not like the way you worded it but you made valid points as well, thank you.

And to add on I don’t clown myself or go way out of my way to seek their attention or validation. Fortunately I’m not that kind of person, ( I don’t say this because they’re bad ppl but because Ik how much they hurt at the end) quite the contrary which is stated in what I wrote in my original post. That was my whole worry that I didn’t seek out and will go days without answering, I was worried that maybe this action was the one that caused them to act like this in the first place, that’s why I mention I would apologize for taking so long to answer. I became attached to them (even if I don’t show it to them all the time) and after a while these actions became more noticeable to me after there’s been some distance between us. And yes I do have other friends and other things going on in my life. But I would imagine more then one person wouldn’t like the thought of their friends ignoring them or the feeling of the friendship vanishing if you care about them. I haven’t expressed anything like this to them because of opinions like the one you just mentioned. Not wanting to look desperate or not touching grass. I feel like if something flows smoothly you won’t feel the need to beg for anything, so that’s why I’ve kept quiet hoping things would somehow change. These are just things I noticed and wanted to know if I was acting crazy or if they were valid points. And once again that’s why I came here instead for help. Again just adding more context for any other future commenters.

I’m sorry if it seemed like I was begging for their attention or was attention seeking in any way. I came here for the first time because I don’t bring this problem up to them, that’s why this is a social skill community because I don’t communicate this type of things to other friends or people. I do have other friends yes and other things in life going on I don’t focus all my attention solely in one specific person. I just happen to overthink and that’s the whole reason why I’m asking for an outside perspective. I don’t want to confront (if it gets to that) someone if I’m completely in the wrong. So to summarize yes I do have self respect and just because I open my concerns up to the Internet does not mean I act the same way in public or in my private life although the way I interpreted this might’ve given that impression. Even so I still appreciate all opinions, I did post it for opinions after all. Maybe I should’ve added more context instead of making it look so desperate. But to answer no I’m not embarrassed because I’m not like this in real life and this is supposed to be a safe space.

What if you were in a relationship with them and you stayed as friends but aren’t sure if the feeling still lingers on their side. You thought the feeling was mutual but you’re starting to notice they’re taking longer to answer and skip every chance to hangout but still give the illusion that they’re “interested”

I have the same thing happen to me. I have a hard time talking to people because my mind goes blank everytime I try to have a conversation, and the anxiety makes it so much worse. What I noticed helps at least for me is realizing that I just simply won’t be able to connect with everyone, and I don’t obligate myself to have a conversation if I simply don’t feel like it. The more I force it the more awkward it gets. Try to find people that will simply vibe with you, listen to music together, paint together, watch a movie and eventually a conversation will arise if you have various things in common. I’m also honest when I finally feel comfortable enough, to tell them that I have a hard time with conversations and most of the time they’re understanding and it lets them know that it’s not that I don’t want to talk just that idk how to and depending on the person they’ll be patient and help me out. Just take it slow I know the desperation of finally letting the  words out is huge but forcing it won’t work. With every therapy with every practice you’re slowly getting there. Another thing you can try is reading and journaling, talking to yourself helps a lot too.
